hypotheses.construction_plan: Extract the diagonal and off-diagonal polygamma coefficient functions D and O from the common first two sums; form the two-parameter family S_{p,q}[D,O] by inserting h1(p,n,m)*h2(a,q,m,n) in place of the h-factors. The observed first sum is obtained for (p,q)=(b,c), the second for (p,q)=(c,b).
required_assumptions: D and O are independent of the labels p,q and are identical across the two double sums.
proof_obligations: S_{p,q}[D,O] with p=b,q=c equals the first double sum exactly.
S_{p,q}[D,O] with p=c,q=b equals the second double sum exactly.
D and O extracted from the two double sums agree branch-by-branch.
hypotheses.rationale: The first two double sums have the same diagonal/off-diagonal coefficient structure but differ only by the permutation of the labels b and c in the h1/h2 prefactors. This is a parameter substitution of a common kernel family.

required_assumptions: The Piecewise coefficient tensor K is identical in both triple sums.
The h1 products are the only structural difference between the two triple sums.
proof_obligations: Branch-by-branch equality of K in the first and second triple sums holds.
T[P1] equals the first triple sum for P1=h1(a,m,n)*h1(b,ell,m)*h1(c,n,ell).
T[P2] equals the second triple sum for P2=h1(a,m,n)*h1(b,n,ell)*h1(c,ell,m).
hypotheses.rationale: The two triple sums share an identical piecewise coefficient structure and differ only in the ordering of the h1 tensor factors, indicating a common coefficient tensor generating different contractions.
